title: On rainbow saturated graphs with minimum number of edges
summary: Let $F$ be a fixed graph without isolated vertices. An edge-colored graph is $F$-rainbow saturated if it contains no rainbow copy of $F$, but the addition of any missing edge in any color creates a rainbow copy of $F$. The rainbow saturation number $rsat(n,F)$ is the minimum number of edges in such a graph on $n$ vertices. We prove a dichotomy governed by isolated edges: if $F$ contains an isolated edge, then $rsat(n,F)=O(1)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, while if $F$ has no isolated edge, then $rsat(n,F)=Θ(n)$.
